_comment: ngsolve linear_elasticity#3 (MatrixValued(..., symmetric=True) stores only the upper triangle). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604 in both 2D (unit_square maxh 0.3) and 3D (unit_cube maxh 0.5) on H1 order 1: full is exactly d^2 times the scalar DOF count (76 = 4*19, 234 = 9*26) and symmetric is exactly d(d+1)/2 times it (57 = 3*19, 156 = 6*26), so the packing claim is arithmetic. The consequence is then exercised: a deliberately non-symmetric tensor with skew-part norm 1.22 comes back from the symmetric space with a skew part of exactly 0.0 -- the space cannot hold it -- while the full space reproduces the same tensor to 2.3e-16. On a genuinely symmetric field the two spaces agree exactly, so the saving costs nothing when the field really is symmetric. Mutation: setting symmetric=False for the sym space makes the DOF counts equal and the fixture fails on 2d_sym_is_half_d_dplus1_times_scalar. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable, INVERTED direction -- this fixture executes no pathology, so the control COMMITS the documented mistake instead of removing it): T2_MUTATE=1 sets SYMMETRIC_PACKING=False, so every 'sym' space is built as MatrixValued(H1(...), symmetric=False) -- the omission this pitfall is about. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 gives sym_ndof 76 (2D) and 234 (3D) instead of 57 and 156 and a retained skew norm of 1.225e+00, so it removes '2d_sym_is_half_d_dplus1_times_scalar=True', '3d_sym_is_half_d_dplus1_times_scalar=True' and 'symmetric_space_cannot_hold_the_skew_part=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear. This is the mutation described earlier in this comment, now executed. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
